items.title: Pressure intensifies on Carrick as Man Utd lose to Bournemouth
items.description: Manchester United's winless run stretches to eight matches in all competitions as they're beaten 3-0 by Bournemouth at Old Trafford - a defeat that leaves United's manager Michael Carrick under severe pressure.

items.title: Liverpool earn first league win at Anfield with victory over Brighton
items.description: An own goal from Brighton's Pascal Gross swiftly followed by a goal from Alexander Isak, sees Liverpool beat the Seagulls 2-0 at Anfield to move into the Premier League top four.

items.title: Sage continues to struggle as Palace lose at home to Newcastle
items.description: Crystal Palace's winless run stretches to four matches as they're beaten 2-0 at home by Newcastle, leaving the club just a point outside the relegation zone with the pressure mounting on manager Pierre Sage.

items.title: Hull draw third consecutive home game after being held by Brentford
items.description: Hull draw a third consecutive home game after Dango Ouattara's equaliser helps Brentford grab a point in a 1-1 draw at the MKM Stadium in the Premier League.

items.title: Sunderland stay bottom after goalless draw with Leeds
items.description: Sunderland remain bottom of the Premier League after a goalless draw with Leeds in difficult conditions at the Stadium of Light.

items.title: Birmingham get first win of the season after edging past Charlton
items.description: Wilda Leidhammar scores as Birmingham secure their first WSL win this season, beating bottom club Charlton 1-0 at St Andrew's, as the away side's wait for a first point goes on.

items.title: Late own goal gives Liverpool point against London City Lionesses
items.description: A stoppage time own goal from Jana Fernandez sees Liverpool snatch a point against London City Lionesses, as the two sides draw 2-2 in the Women's Super League.

items.title: Vangsgaard scores twice as Villa hang on to beat Everton
items.description: Amalie Vangsgaard scores twice for Aston Villa as the away side survive a late fightback from Everton to win 3-2 at Goodison Park in the Women's Super League.

items.title: Weir would swap Ballon d'Or nominations for World Cup
items.description: Caroline Weir reflects on her Ballon d'Or nomination while eyeing a World Cup spot with Scotland.
